subject: Ways to visualize physical position of SNPs?

messages.author: e64f7bb1494774f9
messages.subject: Ways to visualize physical position of SNPs?
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am looking for suggestions on how to visualize SNPs in relation to their physical location on chromosomes or scaffolds. 

gl <- testset.gl
glPlot(gl) is good but doesn't say much about physical location.

Looking in the adegenet tutorials, there is the option to do:

snpposi.plot(position(gl), genome.size=75)

However, it is not completely clear how to set the x-axis such that different chromosomes or regions of interest can be visualized or all visualized similar to a manhattan plot?

Any tips appreciated!

cheers,
Kate

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Ways to visualize physical position of SNPs?
parts:
Hi Kate,

I am not sure that there is a quick way to visualize to location of SNPs on the chromosomes unless you link the sequence tags to an annotated and physically mapped genome. If you have one of these genomes, you can download the NCBI Blast tool and blast your SNP sequence tags to the genome.

DArT can probably do this for you if you nominated a reference genome when requesting your service.

Sorry I cannot be of more help.

Arthur

Hi Arthur, 

Thank you for your input and for your feedback. 

I do have the SNPs and their physical location on scaffolds produced from physically mapped data from NCBI.

I created a numerical dataset that I use for GAPIT. This is how I created the physical location file in case anyone needs it.
Maybe this can be a function in dartR in the future?

rs.subset<-...@loc.names  
#the chrom columns, SNPS chromosome,
chrom.subset<-gl@other$loc.metrics$Chrom_taxa_v1_1 
#the pos which is the SNPs base pair bp psoition
pos.subset<-matrix(gl@other$loc.metrics$ChromPos_taxa_v1_1, ncol=1, byrow=TRUE)
myGM.larv.subset<-as.data.frame(cbind(SNP=rs.subset, Chromosome=chrom.subset, Position=pos.subset))

cheers,
Kate
